findings.text: Lucia and Jason both render, standing together on a night street, with faces, hair and clothes.
A parked car, lit street and the skyline draw behind them: the direction the article calls heading for free roam.
Shadowed detail is still drawn black and geometry sits out of place in both shots.
README: the prologue is playable from the cell to the boat chase — cell, cafeteria, robbery, police chase with wanted level and minimap, boat, binoculars.
README: 1 h 30 min+ in one session without a crash. The 1-3 fps is slower on a first run while shaders translate, then they are cached.
README known problems: shadows black, bright scenes overexposed, ray-traced lighting not running, blocky artifacts, boats sitting low in the water.
Its newest commit adds its own README and a launcher that keeps the shader cache and saves and maps a keyboard to a pad.

Issue 42, RTX 4060 Ti: about 30 minutes without a crash, from the prologue through Chapter I to Jason’s first mission with the plane, at 1 to 3 fps. Screenshots show flat black lighting and corrupted textures. It names no commit.

Issue 55, RTX 5060, with pull requests 36 and 49 and a ray-tracing switch added: the prison yard is reached and lit, input responds, 12 minutes without a crash, 4 to 5 fps. The tester says what is missing still keeps it from being playable.
Issue 16, RTX 4080 on Windows 10, with a VIctory patch added: the lit prison cell at 2.3 fps, and 25 minutes without the card dropping out. Scripted key presses, not a person playing.
Issue 44, RTX 5070: a ten-minute run at about 0.8 fps in the world, without a crash. The one report counted in the score so far.
Issue 46, AMD RX 7600, with four patches added: the prologue at about 2 fps in scripted runs, one of 13 minutes. A later comment says runs do not always survive.
Issues 28 and 39, RTX 5060 and RTX 4060 Ti: two testers hit the same crash about six minutes after entering the world. “Rarely crashes” is the project’s own rating.
Issue 29, RTX 5050: the game stops about a second after launch, before any picture, on every try.
Compared with victory-fork at 2119b0e, ztrx changes two files: its README and a launcher script. The engine code is the same. None of its 36 pull requests had been merged when checked.

to.findingsSource: From Mamozziee’s tweets, the public README and commits, and the testers’ own issue reports, read on 25 November. Code and reports read as text, not run.

findings.text: README v7 reports 25,662 of 25,758 shaders emitted (99.6%) and 25,588 validated, with 25,266 of the 25,662 pipelines accepted on an RTX 5060 Ti (98.5%).
The 396 pipelines the card refuses are compute shaders that need wave64; NVIDIA cards run wave32.
Newest commits add the depth bounds test, faster defaults and textures placed on the card before the character bake.
The README still says the 3D world is not playable: about 3 fps on a first run, shadowed areas dark, and heavy DispatchMesh work can still cause a TDR.

findings.text: Pause map shows the "Gone Fishing" mission, "Help Donnie skim some bricks off a shipment" and "Drive to Cal's house", in Hamlet, South Vice-Dale County, at 7:20 pm with $407.
The map itself draws in colour with roads, coastline, the player marker, a mission marker and the HUD.
An indoor office scene is lit, with an NPC, desk lamp, plant, framed photos and a poster.
Lucia's face and hair render close up in a grey hoodie indoors, and again by a fence in her inmate shirt.
The title bars measure 4 fps through the shots (268.8 to 380.6 ms/frame).
The Gone Fishing boat scene renders Jason and Donnie on a sunlit mangrove river, with water, clouds and birds.
Donnie's yellow cap, sunglasses, moustache and floral shirt render close up, as do Jason's cap, skin and watch.
Glitches: black patches across Jason's shirt and a black sail-like artifact at the boat's edge.
Title bars measure 3.2 to 4.2 fps across the shots.
The boat is being driven down the mangrove river, with a wake, a bridge ahead, the checkpoint route on the minimap (0.45 mi) and the reset prompt. Title bar: 4.5 fps.
The boat shot's title bar names VIctory and reads 4.5 fps (220 ms), 5,308 draws with 108 dropped, 3,016 shaders working and 16 failed, 5 pipelines refused, and 10.0 of 11.7 GB of video memory in use.

A later shot shows a woman from behind on a balcony above palms, a beach and a tower under construction, with lit sky and foliage. Edges are blocky and shadowed areas black. onyx says a PS5 save was reverse engineered to get there and that you could move around, but has no more information. The post doesn't name CGBJ, and a loaded save isn't story progress.

findings.text: The project moved from a personal account to the xcl-dev organisation on GitHub, which the team says helps it coordinate. The old address redirects there.

“65%” is XCL's own figure. It entered the README at 04:53 UTC on 25 November in a pull request whose author calls it an estimate rather than a measurement, about 17 minutes before the post saying XCL leads at 65%. The same collaborator wrote both.

That post gives no evidence for leading. 65% is XCL's estimate of the way to playable; this site's scale starts Playable at 50% and puts XCL at 35%. Entries such as CGBJ, ZETTROX and hyphennn are already past Playable, also self-reported.
The README's 14 fps is one 300-second run on an RTX 5090, with menus and loading screens included. The heaviest scene ran at 5.1 fps, and four other runs averaged 9.3 to 13.2.

The draft branch behind it reaches the world at about 65 seconds, with the radar drawn and the scene still grey, after about an hour of filling shader caches. An earlier revision gave 2 to 3.5 frames a second in the world.

Testers on that draft branch got less far: an RTX 3080 without the caches reached no HUD, an RTX 5080 on Linux saw loading artwork then a uniform screen, and an RX 9070 saw the prologue's first title card in one run of four before a GPU hang.

On an RX 6700 XT, main plus open pull requests and local changes drew the world for about four and a half minutes at 0.5 to 3 fps, once. The saved frames were almost black, and a repeat hung after 19 seconds.
The official roadmap's goal is still to get the game past world loading, and it names shader and pipeline compile time as the biggest obstacle.
BCPack textures now decode for BC1 and BC3 to BC7, checked byte for byte against a reference decoder, the README says. Earlier runs had those requests refused.
A team update reported on X puts optimization, stability and shader speed ahead of 1-2 fps clips, and says XCL is for many games, not one.

On 25 November the README's Discord invite was changed to a second server at 04:31 UTC, without a pull request, and was back on the original by 06:05. A commenter calls the second server a scam. Lead developer ivall says the collaborator believed ivall had lost access and created a new server, and that it is under control.

A Solana coin using XCL's name was promoted in a Discord server on 25 November. Collaborator Austin Ayers calls it a phishing attempt with a fake Discord and fake socials. Who ran it is disputed and not confirmed here. The README doesn't mention a coin.
ivall says no developer was hacked and that “some people were just impersonating us”.

XCL is still active: main was last pushed at 06:05 UTC on 25 November and pull requests are still being updated. The newest merged code is from 02:15; the commits after it edit the README. This site lists a project as inactive after 7 days with nothing new.

to.findingsSource: From XCL’s README, pull requests, issues and commits, and the linked posts on X, on 25 November. Code read as text, not run.

findings.text: myokex's README: the prologue's cutscene and the first room are drawn, with the player moving, at 2 to 3 fps on an RX 7800 XT. Runs of 8 minutes mostly end without a device loss; one hung after about 5.5 minutes.
JoshuuDev's own change is one commit of code, 92 lines in two files: reads from disk now land in a buffer first, so a guarded page no longer fails them.
JoshuuDev's README: without the fix, two runs of two stopped seconds after the world's first frame. With it, one run went 5.5 minutes without a failed read.
Compared with victory-fork it is 12 commits ahead and 5 behind. Nine of the 12 are myokex's, three are JoshuuDev's, and two of those three only change the README.
Brackzmeta’s screenshots are opening cutscene shots: lit faces, hair and clothing with detail, and large areas black. None shows gameplay, a frame rate or a window title.

effort.name: victory-ka1qux
effort.summary: An AMD-focused fork of hyphennn's victory-fork, developed on one Radeon RX 7800 XT. Its README reports the world drawn with textures and direct light, and a 25-minute session to the next objective, at about 2 fps. Self-reported.

findings.text: README: rooms, exteriors, characters with skin, hair and clothes, HUD and prompts are drawn from a save on an RX 7800 XT. Light that the sun or a lamp does not give directly is missing.

README: a median of 0.50 s a frame over a ten-minute run, about 2 fps. victory-fork's speed defaults gave about 3.5 fps in one run on an earlier build, but are left off because an earlier version of them cost characters their skin.
README: no crash or device removal in the last 24 runs, of 4 to 25 minutes each. Nobody else has reported the same yet.
Its own code includes splitting dispatches of more than 65,535 groups into parts (the game asks for 115,200 in its indirect-light pass), with tests for the split.
Compared with victory-fork it was 137 commits ahead and none behind. 39 of them, merges aside, are ka1qux's, some applying other people's pull requests, which the README credits by number.

The 47-second video shared on X shows the opening scenes, lit, with shadows going black, one shot blown out to white and the first room's walls arriving late. A title bar reads 2 fps. It shows cutscenes, not the player in control.
The same post says the work targets AMD RDNA3 cards and that updates will be fewer because of Rockstar's DMCA. Its reply links this repo.

effort.name: DumbFloridaMoron
effort.summary: CRT's fork of VIctory and hyphennn's victory-fork, with many open VIctory pull requests merged. Opening scenes draw at about 3 to 6.6 fps. CRT told us Lucia can be moved at the start; no recording shows it yet. Self-reported.

findings.text: CRT's post of 24 November, 19:24 UTC, has a 122-second video: start-up, first-boot settings, a long load, then the story intro's titles and subtitles over an empty dark picture. The post puts the starting point at XCL merged with VIctory, and the target at mobile NVIDIA graphics.
CRT's post of 24 November, 22:37 UTC, shows a page listing CRT's own posts: one of 24 November on NVIDIA work for GTA VI, one of 21 November on not reverse engineering it. It does not show the build.

CRT's release post of 25 November, 00:49 UTC, calls it unplayable, unstable and experimental: menus at 30 fps, the world loads, the story starts, no ray tracing yet. Four shots show opening scenes with sky and characters, but missing body parts, floating geometry and mostly empty ground.

CRT's post of 25 November, 08:17 UTC, “7hrs later”, shows Lucia in a cutscene, lit, with skin, hair and fabric detail. A garbled white patch sits behind her, and the rest of the room is mostly black. No frame rate is shown.
README: 5.6 to 6.6 fps in the first world scenes and about 3 fps in the heavy intro scene, up from 0.5 to 1.9. We score the lower figure.
README: 120 to 270 draws a frame are dropped because two console pipeline methods are not written. The ray-tracing builder translates, but shadowed areas still come out dark.
README: all 26,142 GPU programs translate to DXIL. That says they convert, not that their output is right, and it earns no credit here.
Its history holds merges of 76 different VIctory pull requests; one of them, 436, was reverted later. 45 other commits are CRT's own work or ports from other forks.
